horses.spotlight_comment: Many of these have a point to prove and it may pay to focus on the 4yo contenders. Ted Le Saux had an excuse (irregular heartbeat post race) at Wolverhampton and can step forward now handicapping, while Winter Flower (second choice) will appreciate dropping back down in class. CAVOLO NERO wasn't seen to best effect upped in trip 17 days ago and this may pan out more favourably. He looks well handicapped judged on his earlier Kempton second.[Paul Smith] Page 4 spotlighthaydock 25.04.26

Those from the highest-profile yards, Commanding Officer (second choice) for Charlie Appleby and Go Rimbaud for the Gosdens, inevitably attract immediate interest, having won their most recent starts. However,

has not had to exert himself unduly to win both his handicaps and a 4lb rise for his Musselburgh win doesn't look too harsh. See Blue could turn out the pick of the remainder.[Emily Weber] Page 5 spotlighthaydock 25.04.26

horses.spotlight_comment: Cherry Cobbler threatened to be a cut above this grade at one stage and a return to form could be forthcoming now he's dropped back to 6f in a 0-70 and with cheekpieces added. He is making his turf debut, however, and he could be drawn away from the best pace so he is overlooked for the win, albeit cautiously. FISCAL POLICY ran a fine race at Thirsk on his return to turf two weeks ago and he could be the answer off the same mark. Punchbowl Flyer may prove best of the rest, although keep an eye on Harry Mole too.[Paul Smith] Page 7
